To Oli + his agents · 17 August 2026

cdp + workchain, and what it turned up

I started with CDP doing what CDP does, then adding one layer at a time until the engine is doing things CDP has no equivalent for. Each section says plainly what is gained, including the first one, where the answer is nothing.

Everything here was executed against cdp-wasm 0.6.0. Every duration, frame count, digest and distance is read out of a run artifact. Sources are synthesised rather than sampled, so the whole thing is shareable.

engine LUFS Workchain · @lufs-audio/workchain 0.1.0 · github.com/lufs-audio/workchain
CDP cdp-wasm 0.6.0 sources struck metal bar (B♭3, 1.6s) · shaker (0.45s) · plucked string (D3, 1.8s)

Act I · just CDP

Your catalog, driven from a text file

A chain is YAML. A step names an effect and its values, and the engine resolves parameters, runs the render, and passes the result to the next step. At this level Workchain is a just a solid runner, and cdp is the driver. Your programs, doing what they already do.

01

Bloom stretch.time

A 0.45-second shaker hit stretched eightfold. The transient becomes an envelope and the noise becomes pitch. classic CDP.

factor 80.45s → 3.805s26 checks

02

Spectral wash stretch.time

The struck bar held open for ten seconds. You can see the strike smeared across the whole duration and the partials sustained where they had been decaying.

factor 61.6s → 9.749s26 checks

03

Dissolve blur.blur

The window count is driven by a breakpoint envelope rather than a constant, so the string dissolves across its own decay instead of being uniformly blurred.

windows 1 → 80, breakpoint envelope1.8s → 1.823s19 checks

04

Spectral trace hilite.trace

Keep the six loudest partials in each analysis window, everything else discarded.

partials 61.6s → 1.622s19 checks

Gained so far: not much, any of these is four lines of js against your api.

Act II · the first thing you gain

A step that cannot report success without evidence

Every component declares a contract, and a single verifier re-measures the artifact after the run. For the CDP wrapper that is eleven checks: the output exists, decodes, and carries real audio above a liveness floor; every value supplied was inside the catalog's declared range; any breakpoint envelope was actually staged and applied rather than silently ignored; and the render is reproducible. A step passes only when all of them hold.

The check I care most about is the envelope one, since a knob that accepts a curve and quietly ignores it is worse than a knob that is absent, because you cannot hear the difference between a subtle envelope and no envelope at all.

Two layers, independently

Driving stretch.time to 0.02 — the zero-frame case from the issue. The wrapper validates against your catalog before any audio is touched, so the chain halts and names the range:

cdp_transform: refusing to process: 1 out-of-range and 0 unknown parameter(s) for 'stretch.time':
    factor=0.02 — outside the catalog curated range (0.25..8)

And going around the wrapper entirely, calling applyEffect directly, 0.6.0 catches it itself:

threw — stretch.time produced a WAV with no audio frames. CDP can write an empty
output without reporting an error when a parameter is far outside its declared
range — check the values against the catalog's min/max.

Neither layer needs the other, which imo is exactly the right arrangement. And on the design question, re-running the whole threshold table against 0.6.0:

factor  0.03 → 1280 frames   0.04 → 1664   0.05 → 2176   0.10 → 4352
        0.25 → 11136 (declared min)      2 → 90240

Every one of those below 0.25 still produces audio, with frame counts identical to 0.5.3. Validating against the curated range would have rejected all of them. The output guard catches the failure without charging for it.

Gained: a step that cannot lie about its own output — and, for an agent driving the tool unattended, a failure that arrives as a refusal rather than as a silent file nobody listens to.

Act III · what measurement buys

Transforms become comparable to each other

Once a render is an artifact under contract, you can measure it. Eleven effects on the same struck bar, each result measured twice: deterministic DSP features, and a 64-dimension L2-normed embedding. Because the embedding contract guarantees the norm, cosine distance is meaningful — so “how far did this effect move the sound” becomes a number you can sort by.

The two measurements corroborate each other, which is the only reason either is worth reporting. blur.suppress removes the twelve loudest partials, so the centroid climbs +2276 Hz — what remains is what was quiet and high. hilite.pluck emphasises onsets, and a struck bar's onset already dominates, so it barely moves the sound at all: distance 0.0000, centroid +10 Hz. That agreement is what separates a measurement from a number.

Gained: a catalog you can navigate by intent. You or an agent asks for “something that keeps the identity of this sound” can pick from the bottom of that list, and one asked to destroy it can pick from the top, without a human having auditioned 232 effects first. The embedding here is a dependency-light stand-in rather than CLAP, behind a fixed vector contract — the numbers are real, but they are not yet CLAP numbers.

Act IV · past the edge of CDP

A render becomes something you can find again

One chain, five steps, 30 checks: cdp_transform → probe → features → embed → hook. The transform is one step of five, and the other four have no CDP equivalent at all — they are what turns a file in a folder into an entry in a library.

probe

content hash 91c779b0ccc952bf5092e80a…
catalog no. lufs-91c779b0
duration 1.6225s · peak -8.8 dBFS
decoder ffmpeg

features

centroid 3533.61 Hz
rolloff85 4345.67 Hz
rms -35.35 dBFS
zcr 0.35041 · brightness 0.3205

embed

model melstats-v0
dim 64 · l2 norm 1.0
vector [64 floats]

and a hook, so a library is browsable by ear

The hook step finds the loudest window and cuts three seconds from it, with a waveform to match. At a few hundred thousand files, filenames stop being a way to find anything and auditioning becomes the only interface that works.

Gained: the render has identity. It has provenance, a measured description, a position in a vector space, and something you can hear in 3 seconds. So the next question can be “find me the others like this” rather than “what did I call that file”.

Two smaller notes

Observed in passing

grain.reverse gave no output on any source I tried

Four synthetic sources — 1.0s and 3.0s at 233 Hz, 1.0s at 80 Hz, 0.5s at 440 Hz — each returned grain produced no output (exit -1) with an ERROR: INVAL underneath. Seems right but might be worth the message naming that: the grain programs segment on amplitude troughs and a smooth decaying sine has no grain onsets, so zero grains may be exactly correct.

hardMin / hardMax are declared by one effect of 232

We expose an “unlock the range” switch that falls back to the engine hard limits where the catalog records them, and in practice only rotor.rotor does, so for everything else the curated range remains the effective limit even when unlocked. Seems like maybe a data-coverage observation though, rather than a bug.

Close

Curious on where you think a contract belongs.

You put the guard at the output because the curated range is meant to be leaveable. That is a judgement about where truth is cheapest to establish, and it is the same judgement every component in our engine has to make. I would like to know how you would draw that line across 232 programs rather than one.

Chain topology. Your cdp-sound-design patch format distinguishes linear, two-input and graph. We arrived at the same three categories from the other direction and are currently linear-only, with two-input next. Converging independently on the same taxonomy suggests it is the real shape of the problem.

Similarity and tagging. Act III is a placeholder embedding behind a fixed contract, and the interesting version swaps it for CLAP over a large personal archive. This is where I'm currently heading, and I suspect you may have already gleaned some insights about it.
